findings.evidence: Lines 51–64 use only `LinearEquiv.continuous_baseChange` and subtype continuity. That theorem requires `[CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L]` and `[ContinuousMul (Module.End K V)]`; `orthogonalGroupBaseChange` is defined over commutative rings, while `specialOrthogonalGroupBaseChange` additionally requires `Module.Free` and `Module.Finite`.
findings.fix: State the orthogonal theorem over commutative rings with `[ContinuousMul (Module.End K V)]`; give the special-orthogonal theorem the same signature plus `[Module.Free K V] [Module.Finite K V]`, as required by its algebraic base-change map.
findings.issue: Both continuity theorems assume fields, `IsTopologicalRing K`, and `FiniteDimensional K V`, although their proofs only consume continuity of linear-equivalence base change; this excludes the natural commutative-ring/module setting already supported by the algebraic maps.

summary: The orthogonal specializations unnecessarily restrict the generic continuity theorem to finite-dimensional vector spaces over fields.
